limitations: Behaviour labels come from rule-based heuristics on pose and COCO object cues, not from trained instructor / student behaviour models.
Roles come from the calibration zones: anyone inside the teacher zone is treated as the instructor.

The calibration assumes a fixed camera. If the camera pans, zooms or cuts to a close-up, the instructor can fall outside the teacher zone and be labelled a student, so events in those segments are unreliable.
Seat IDs are grid cells, so crowded or moving students can share or switch seats.
Writing cannot be told apart from looking down, so note-taking may count as off-task.
Board writing needs a raised wrist and interaction needs facing plus a raised wrist; both rules are strict and unvalidated, so zero counts can mean a missed behaviour.
Frames are sampled every 2 s, so short actions can be missed.

glossary.observable students: Seats where a student's head and shoulders were readable in the video. Not every student in the room.
glossary.focused: Head up rather than looking down. A posture proxy; it is not a measure of attention, understanding or learning.
glossary.explaining to the class: The instructor was visible, facing the students, and not writing on the board.
glossary.not facing the class: The instructor was visible but not turned toward the students or the board.
glossary.moving around: The most mobile quarter of windows, by how far the instructor travelled.
glossary.close to the students: The quarter of windows where the instructor was closest to the nearest student.
glossary.seated: The instructor's thighs looked short beside the torso (needs hips and knees in view).
glossary.evidence.strength: weak = the gap could easily be chance; suggestive = unlikely to be pure chance; descriptive = a single observation or a count, not a test.

alternative_explanations.E1: Students may have looked down to write notes, which the head-up rule counts as not focused.
alternative_explanations.E2: Students may have been reading a slide or the board rather than watching the instructor.
alternative_explanations.E3: The camera moves in this recording, so some people may have been mislabelled or out of view.
alternative_explanations.E4: The comparison rests on a small number of 10-second windows.
alternative_explanations.E5: The type of activity (lecture, seat-work, discussion) was not recorded, and it changes posture on its own.
